chapter: The Los Angeles music scene in the early 1930s
title: Men's attitude to women instrumentalists; Valaida Snow
summary: He says men thought women pianists lacked a strong left hand and voicing, and that women played few other instruments; he barely knew Valaida Snow.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Mr. Blakeney, tell us a bit about the interaction between the male and the female musicians during this
time. What was the attitude of the men musicians towards the women?

The attitude then was that the woman pianist wasn't quite as strong as the men would like them to be, especially as the background, the left hand chords; it wasn't as good as the average man. A man understood more than the average woman.
Was this so with Mrs. Hightower and Mrs. Butler?
Do you think that the men musicians were concerned as to whether or not they were male or female?
Some of the musicians were, they figured a woman pianist wasn't heavy enough, especially on the voicing of the cords.
At this time were there any women playing other instruments in the band, that you recall?
Mostly pianist. I liked one that came up--I can't think of her name.
Was Miss Snow ever in the California area, that you recall?
Yes, back in that time she was around, but mostly with shows that she was with.
She was like a specialty act?
Something like that, yes. Valaida Snow; I don't remember too much about her personally. I don't remember ever working with her.
